meta.title: $\pi$ Shift Bragg Grating for Acousto Optic Sensing: Research Overview
meta.subtitle: What raises $Q$ at a fixed 20\,$\mu$m mode, and what does not
meta.author: Evyatar Rubin

frames.title: Bottom line
items: Benchmark: a 20\,$\mu$m mode lengthened to a $-3$\,dB peak; compare $Q$.
Changing the teeth trades loss against mode width; cavity and lateral structures do not.
TM radiates sideways: a trench or SiN post row raises $Q$ by a third; TE does not respond.
Inverse design at fixed width: about 6$\times$, in progress, below the lab's overshoot.

frames.heading: Details
frames.subheading: TE, TE versus TM, TM levers, inverse design

frames.title: TE: apodization cuts loss and widens the mode
items: Linear apodization: loss down, mode much wider. Tanh: same gain, less widening.
A few apodized periods are enough; more add nothing.
The lab's overshoot apodization is stronger by far: only its amplitude sets the mode width.

frames.title: TE: shifting the innermost teeth recycles the leak
items: Shifting the innermost teeth outward cuts loss; the mode width stays.
Light that would leak at the cavity is redirected into the mode; the far field collapses to one lobe.
A two tooth particle swarm design gave the best transmission per width; fabricated devices confirmed the shift range.

frames.title: TE versus TM
items: Same length: TM couples more weakly, so less loss, lower $Q$, wider mode.
Same peak transmission: TM is longer and its $Q$ is about three times higher.
At the operating point the plain gratings tie. TM radiates in the propagation plane, TE upward.

frames.title: TM: the teeth behave as in TE, except the shift
items: Apodization: loss down, mode wider.
A large innermost shift widens the mode with no optimum; TM does not recycle at the cavity.
A wider cavity cuts loss with the mode width unchanged.

frames.title: TM: an air trench raises $Q$ by a third
text: The trench returns the in plane radiation by total internal reflection; the mode width is unchanged.
A trench stopping at the core top keeps most of the gain in one lithography step.
A deep etch conflicts with the PDMS cover, hence the post rows.

frames.title: TM: a row of SiN posts does the trench's job
items: The row is a weak grating: its period sets the beam angle, $n_\text{clad}\sin\theta = n_\text{eff} - \lambda/\Lambda$.
Aimed at the radiation lobe, sliding the row sets the phase: one phase cancels the lobe, the opposite grows it.
A second row on the other side adds a few percent; a third adds nothing.

frames.title: Inverse design: in progress
items: Adjoint optimization of the 25 innermost teeth per side and the cavity, TM.
Peak transmission is maximized with the mode width and the resonance held fixed.
About 6$\times$ the plain grating so far. Next: more free teeth, then a TE run seeded from the overshoot profile.
